newsitem.title: USA: Neoprobe in sales pact with U.S. Surgical.
newsitem.headline: Neoprobe in sales pact with U.S. Surgical.

text.p: Neoprobe Corp on Thursday said it signed a deal under which U.S. Surgical Corp gained exclusive worldwide sales and marketing rights for Neoprobe's RIGS products for surgical cancer detection.
The agreement, which excludes Korea, Thailand, Taiwan and Singapore, became effective September 18, Neoprobe said.

U.S. Surgical will pay Neoprobe $5.5 million, the majority of which will be paid upon U.S. and European marketing approval of RIGScan CR49, Neoprobe's first RIGS product, for surgical detection of metastatic colorectal cancer.
No exchange of equity is involved in the agreement, Dublin, Ohio-based Neoprobe said.

In an interview, Neoprobe president David Bupp said the the company expected to file with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in the fourth quarter, with final approval possible in 1997's third quarter. Final European approval could come in the first half of next year, he said.
Neoprobe retains primary responsibility for product development and manufacturing.
U.S. Surgical will provide surgeon training and professional education worldwide for RIGS products, upon marketing approval, and will help fund future research.
It also has has options on future RIGS surgical detection products for the next five years, Neoprobe said.
Bupp said future products would include those for the detection of breast, prostate and upper gastro-intestinal cancers.
Bupp said Neoprobe will book sales of the products, with U.S. Surgical getting a "sales commission" in the form of a percentage of revenues. He declined to give the percentage.
In a statement, Norwalk, Conn.-based U.S. Surgical said it expects the deal to be accretive within the first year.

The RIGS system works by injecting patients with Neoprobe's low-energy radioactive drug that targets cancer cells. A surgeon uses the hand-held RIGS probe which emits an tone when it has located tissue containing a significant amount of the radioactive targeting agent.
Bupp said target pricing for the drug was $1,500, which would mean a worldwide market of $600 million for the colorectal product.

Under the deal Neoprobe will know get information on RIGS customers, who will be potential buyers for the company's future therapy products, Bupp said. U.S. Surgical does not have rights to the therapy products under the deal, he said.
